23: ## Overview
24: 
25: Players lead families seeking reputation through the East India Company. The Company is collectively operated by the players who hold its offices. Family wealth funds enterprises, politics and retirements; Company funds belong to individual offices and cannot be spent as family cash. Victory points, rather than cash or Company profitability, determine the winner.
26: 
27: **Scope:** Complete standard multiplayer rules, including the 1710, 1758, 1813 and Long 1710 scenarios and the core deregulation/firm system. This uses the Second Edition rules, not the 2017 edition. The Crown solo/two-player system (Rules pp43–46 and separate Crown Handbook), its difficulty settings, and the optional setup-card Draft variant are excluded. Deregulation is part of the standard advanced scenarios and is included here. Card-specific powers, restrictions, starting holdings and scenario map configurations are read from the relevant components.
28: 
29: ## Components
30: 
31: - Board: prizes, Company Balance/Debt/Standing, Court and Stock Exchange, offices and treasuries, Power/Vote/VP/Turn tracks, India and three sea zones. Follow the red ribbon to operate offices.
32: - Six families: each has 18 family members, VP marker, five promise cards, opportunity marker, family board/firm charter, two firm cubes and four strategy cards.
33: - Enterprises: 22 shipyards, 20 workshops and 16 luxuries; 20 prestige and 10 blackmail cards; 26 laws, six Company failure cards; scenario and player setup cards; 17 office cards, Governor/China/Governor General overlays.
34: - India: towers and domes, three sets of empire flags, eight loot/control tokens, Elephant, event tiles, closed/filled order tokens and Presidency dividers. Military and shipping: officers represented by family pieces, regiments, local alliances, player ships and Company/extra ships. Also fatigue/unrest cubes, trophies/passed-law tokens, money, ordinary dice and storm die.
35: 
36: **Limits:** Components are limited: when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information, including discards and family cash, is public except facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids during selection.
37: 
38: **India terminology:** A region's tower levels are its strength; the dome adds none. Orders are connected trading opportunities with printed revenue values; heavy outlines mark home ports. Closed orders cannot be filled. Sovereign regions have a dome without a flag or a capital/star flag; dominated regions have a small flag or no dome. An empire has one capital and at least one dominated region. **Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital's starred flag: it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of that last dominated region.** Presidencies are Bombay, Madras and Bengal, each with its own treasury, writers, fleet, Army and associated Company regions.
39: 
40: The Elephant is always in play. On a border, its tail is the acting region and its head the target. A sovereign actor threatens Invasion; a dominated actor facing its sovereign threatens Rebellion. An Elephant fully inside a Company region threatens Rebellion there.
41: 
42: ## Setup
43: 
44: 1. Set out board and supplies. Shuffle India events. Put local alliances in their named Army boxes. Set Balance to £5, Power tokens on their indicated starting positions, family VP markers to zero, loot tokens money-side up in matching regions.
45: 2. Choose a scenario and follow its setup card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and the political map of India. Put the Turn marker on its date and point the PM dial's arm to the matching date. The scenario determines its final turn.
46: 3. Use that scenario's player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six for six players. Shuffle and deal evenly. **Place every listed holding:** take cash from the bank and enterprise cards into your area; put each office's family member in its office and give its matching office card to that owner; put Company-share members in Court of Directors; put writers, officers and trainees in their indicated Presidency/Army/Training boxes; put a Commander in that Army's Commander slot **without an office card**; take each shipyard and put its matching ship in the **listed sea zone**, or **on its shipyard if unfitted**. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP.
47: 4. Set remaining office cards nearby, distinguishing vacant offices from offices not yet created. Shuffle **prestige and blackmail together into ONE deck**; deal three for the London Season display, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown. Shuffle remaining laws. Keep family and firm pieces near each player.
48: 
49: | Scenario | Standard scope |
50: |---|---|
51: | 1710 | Recommended first game; Company monopoly, without deregulation procedures. |
52: | 1758 | Company starts with monopoly; deregulation can be voted in. |
53: | 1813 | Starts deregulated, allowing firms; recommended with five or six players. |
54: | Long 1710 | Same initial position as 1710, with deregulation available; can run eight turns, often twice the normal length. |
55: 
56: **Scenario figures (official setup cards and board):**
57: 
58: | Scenario | Turns | Initial Standing / Debt | Each office treasury | Initial laws | Initial military and Company ships |
59: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
60: | 1710 | 1–5 | £10 expectations / 0 | £3 | Royal Protection | One regiment per Army; no Company ships. |
61: | Long 1710 | 1–8 | Same as 1710 | £3 | Royal Protection; Deregulation available separately | Same as 1710. |
62: | 1758 | 3–7 | £12 expectations / 3 | £4 | Calico Acts | One regiment per Army; one Company ship in East Indian. Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency. |
63: | 1813 | 5–8 | £10 expectations / 0 | £3 | Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor's Prison side), Calico Acts | Two regiments per Army; one Company ship per sea zone. |
64: 
65: In 1813, put **+2/−2 share-value token** in Court, create China, place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies, return the **Governor General law** to the box and place its office overlay over Director of Trade. Use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors. Copy the exact India towers, flags, closed orders and Elephant from the scenario card's reverse; 1758 includes the Bengal Governor overlay. Starting player-owned ships and offices come from the dealt setup cards in addition to these figures.
66: 
67: **Initial Power positions, from lowest to highest:** Manufacturing 0 → Shipping 0 → Company shares 1 → Social 2. The two zero-Power spaces are distinct ordered positions; Manufacturing starts below Shipping. Standing expectations run £4/6/8/10/12/14/16; reset S is above £10. For Deregulation, **lined** Standing £4/6/8 or Debt 5/6/7/8 **PERMITS the PM to call** the special vote; **starred** Standing £4 or Debt 8 **REQUIRES the PM to call** it.
68: 
69: ### Prizes: cost, upkeep, VP and windows
70: 
71: Values below are per family member.
72: 
73: | Cost | Upkeep | VP | Windows |
74: |---|---|---|---|
75: | £2 | £0 | 0 | 0 |
76: | £4 | £1 | 2 | 1 |
77: | £8 | £2 | 4 | 2 |
78: | £14 | £3 | 8 | 3 |
79: | £20 | £4 | 12 | 4 |

81: ## Turn Structure
82: 
83: Each game turn follows: **London Season → Family → Firms (if deregulated) → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh.** Skip London Season on the game's first turn. Eligible special Deregulation votes occur at the very start of the turn, before London Season.
84: 
85: ### I. London Season (Rules pp11–12)
86: 
87: **Attrition:** Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.
88: 
89: **Retirements:** Starting with the Chairman (former Chairman if vacant), clockwise, each player may retire each pensioner to a prize. Pay its printed cost, move the member to the prize and gain printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display-selection order, then pay bank. Prizes may incur upkeep and window taxes. Unused pensioners do not remain for another turn.
90: 
91: **Prestige:** Players who completed at least one pensioner retirement **or an eligible firm special retirement during this London Season** must each take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. A firm special retirement uses a supply member instead of a pensioner but otherwise counts as a normal retirement for this selection; each eligible player still selects only one card. Ties: most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. Acting player may peek at display blackmails. **Do not replace a chosen/discarded card during selection. If the display becomes empty, immediately skip every remaining eligible player.** Finish the display step by **discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three: prestige faceup, blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card**. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.
92: 
93: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Make required enterprise/share trades immediately upon taking the spouse. Retirement discounts can stack, are personal, and each is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring. Discounts reduce actual spending and therefore display priority. **Returned shipyard rule:** whether a shipyard is returned because of Violet Effingham or an unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; purchase becomes possible after the ship returns.
94: 
95: Prestige enterprises retain their type, power and policy effects and can be traded. Blackmail has a one-time printed effect: once used, place it faceup in its owner's area; it can no longer be traded. Both faceup and facedown blackmail can contribute its printed power at final scoring.
96: 
97: ### II. Family (Rules pp13–14)
98: 
99: Starting with the Chairman title holder, clockwise, each player resolves their family action:
100: 
101: 1. Check where your opportunity marker was **at phase start** (it begins off the board).
102: 2. Choose a main family action: take it once, or **may take it twice if the marker already matched it**.
103: 3. **Place/move the opportunity marker onto your chosen main action.**
104: 4. After the main action, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant its extra action. This extra action is never doubled by the marker and never moves the marker.
105: 
106: If placing a family piece with none in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize's printed VP. This applies to firm-share creation too. If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.
107: 
108: | Family action | Effect |
109: |---|---|
110: | Enlist Writer | Place a member in any Presidency's Writers box. With at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer **once this turn**, so a doubled Writer action can place three total. |
111: | Enlist Officer | Place a member in Officers-in-Training. |
112: | Purchase Luxury | Pay bank £4; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned, and its window icon; social enterprise. |
113: | Purchase Shipyard | Pay bank £2; take shipyard and place its matching ship **unfitted on that shipyard**, not in a sea zone. Shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. |
114: | Purchase Workshop | Pay bank £5; take workshop; manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus; worth 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. |
115: | Seek Share | Place a member on an empty Stock Exchange space and pay bank: the five queue spaces are £2, £3, £3, £4, £5 (two distinct £3 spaces). It is an applicant, not yet a share. |
116: 
117: **New Company shares:** After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both remain. Pieces in Court are Company shares. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries.
118: 
119: ### III. Hiring (Rules pp14–16)
120: 
121: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; its owner gets the card. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists, or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
122: 
123: **Own-family hiring needs verbal consent from every other player in that office's candidate pool, EXCEPT that a Chairman election never requires Nepotism consent. Commander appointments are also exempt.**
124: 
125: **Nepotism and its exceptions:**
126: 
127: | Selection | Own-family consent requirement |
128: |---|---|
129: | Ordinary office hire | Verbal consent from **every other player represented in that office's candidate pool**. |
130: | Chairman election, including deadlock fallback | **Exempt from Nepotism**; use the shareholder election/fallback rules. |

146: ### IV. Company Operation
147: 
148: Follow the red ribbon left to right: **Chairman → Director of Trade (or Governor General) → Manager of Shipping → Military Affairs → Bombay Presidency → Madras Presidency → Bengal Presidency → China Superintendent, if created**. Skip each vacant office. **Within EACH Presidency, its President chooses the order of its Commander, Governor(s) and Trade; each position finishes before the next acts.** Each office spends only its own treasury. Offices created by actions go into Vacant Offices unless immediate hiring is specified. A newly created Governorship normally awaits a later Hiring phase.
149: 
150: **Success checks (p17):** First commit resources/cash: **all cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank**. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll. Use lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 catastrophic failure, no more office actions, return officeholder to supply, discard fatigue and flip card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures modify this. You cannot take a dead action with no effect or chance of success: for example trade with no ship or deploy without dice to trigger possible officer losses.
151: 
152: Office procedures are in **Actions** below. Presidency order is Bombay, Madras, Bengal; each President orders its own Commander, Governor(s) and Trade. China acts after Bengal.
153: 
154: ### V. Bonuses (p27)
155: 
156: Each player takes £1 per workshop and per shipyard whose ship is fitted. Invested workshops give no bonus. Transferring an enterprise cannot trigger its bonus a second time.
157: 
158: ### VI. Revenue (p27; firms pp41–42)
159: 
160: If deregulated, firms pay expenses/dividends first. Then Company:
161: 
162: 1. **Expenses:** Reduce Balance £1 per existing Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones, including China. Exclude Commanders. If insufficient, take £5 emergency loans. Each loan advances Debt one **only while a track space remains**. **At maximum Debt, keep taking loans without advancing Debt any further.** Newly added emergency Debt causes no extra current-turn expense. After using emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower Standing two.
163: 2. **Expectations:** Compare remaining Balance to the expectations under **current** Standing; if lower, lower Standing one.
164: 3. **Dividends:** Chairman may pay any affordable number. Each dividend costs one cash per Company share; pay each owner £1 per share, including Chairman. **Company shareholders cannot waive payment.** If total cash paid as dividends is **strictly greater** than expectations, advance Standing one space.
165: 
166: Standing reaching leftmost space means Company failure. During Revenue, go immediately to Final Scoring.
167: 
168: ### VII. Events in India (pp28–33)
169: 
170: **First roll the storm die:** a sea-zone result affects **that zone**, three storms affects **ALL sea zones**, and no storm indication means **NO storm checks**. The die face also specifies the **number of India events**. Resolve all required storms **before drawing any event**. Then flip and resolve **one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as the number printed on that die face**. Where an event uses a region, normally read the **back of the new top tile** in the draw stack, not the tile just drawn; follow each event's specific location rule.
171: 
172: **Storms:** Determine eligibility in the zone(s) specified above before rolling:
173: 
174: | Ships | Storm exposure |
175: |---|---|
176: | Company and extra ships | **Exempt**; never roll storm checks. |
177: | Player-owned ships in Company fleets | Check ships in the affected sea zone(s). |
178: | Ships assigned to China | Count as **Eastern** sea zone. |
179: | Firm ships | Count in the sea zone on their **firm strategy**, even though on a charter. |
180: | Hobnob firm ships | **Exempt** from storms. |
181: 
182: Roll **once per eligible ship**: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Return a sunk ship to its shipyard **unfatigued**.
183: 
184: **Closing orders and Cascades:** Return any writer on a newly closed order to its owner's supply; flip a filled token to closed. If told to close an order in an already fully closed region, Cascade: close all open orders directly connected to that region's orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region's northernmost open order instead. If none are open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate a Cascade only once per event tile but can receive multiple Cascades' effects.

189: | Windfall | Owners take £1 per writer on orders in top-stack region and every bordering region. |

653: Concepts and Key Terms
654: Component Limits and Infinite Tracks
655: Most components in John Company are limited by the pieces included. If a supply 
656: of pieces is empty, complete as much of the action as possible. However, players may 
657: use proxies if they run out of cash, trophy/passed law tokens, dice, and regiments. 
658: The Company Balance, Victory Point, and Vote tracks have no limit. 
659: Your Play Area and Hidden Information
660: Players maintain a play area that contains everything they own. All information 
661: (including the contents of discard piles) is public except facedown blackmail cards.
662: Cash Flow
663: In John Company, cash always has a location, and its location determines how it 
664: can be spent, traded, or paid. You can spend cash in your family treasury on various 
665: family actions, retirements, upkeep, taxes, and negotiations. Cash within a Company 
666: office can only be spent by that office. 
667: Some Company positions will reward players with extra income during their actions. 
668: In the rules, these payments are highlighted by boxes like this one.
669: The Presidencies
670: The British East India Company divided India into three administrative zones called 
671: Presidencies which are each named after their home region. In John Company, these 
672: Presidencies are special offices that maintain their own Army, cadre of writers, fleet of 
673: ships, and—later in the game—subordinate offices. These resources are stored in their 
674: marked boxes or in the zone of the Indian Ocean near their office box on the map.
675: The Map of India and How to Read It
676: Though much of the action of John Company occurs outside of India, players will

5: 
6: Hello everyone!
7: 
8: I'm happy to report that John Company will be in your hands shortly. Behind the scenes, Drew and I have been very busy preparing the game for language localization. Part of this process involves combing through the forums and making sure we can catch and fix any little errors that snuck through our editorial process. 
9: 
10: In the coming weeks, I'll be posting a full list of all of the little errors we caught (there are a dozen or so small typos throughout and a few statements that required clarification or expansion). These errors won't stop you from enjoying the game and they are minor enough that we won't be offering anything like an correction pack. Eventually we'll be providing a link in this thread to our comprehensive tracking document so that you can see them all if you'd like.
11: 
12: In the meantime, I wanted to highlight a few small points of errata.
13: 
14: [size=18]Omissions[/size]
15: [i]One of the perils of doing a lot of development on TTS is that we automated setup very early in the process and a few setup steps got missed in the rules. Thankfully they are at least fairly easy to remember and implement. [/i]
16: 
17: [b]General Setup:[/b]
18: + [New Step] Place the loot tokens in the matching regions.
19: + [Adjusted Step 4] Clarify that a "Set of family pieces" also includes the family board. 
20: 
21: [b]1758 Setup:[/b]
22: + Place the Bengal control token in the Bengal Presidency. 
23: 
24: [b]1813 Setup:[/b]
25: + Place the Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in the Presidencies of the same name.
26: + Place the +2/-2 Company Share Value token in the Court of Directors. 
27: 
28: [b]Family Actions[/b]
29: + Enlist Officers: The Officers-in-Training box is the box with the Officers-in-Training icon (pistol over building that matches the action icon).
30: + Seek Shares: The stock exchange track refers to the track above the Board of Directors. 
31: 
32: [size=18]Clarifications[/size]
33: [b]Rulebook:[/b]
34: +Commander Rules: You cannot deploy in regions already associated with another Presidency.
35: +Region Loss: Regions that are lost are no long associated with their presidency.
36: +Elephant's March: In the third bullet point (when marching to a region that is already sovereign) the wording has been adjusted to harmonize better with the Imperial Ambitions rule as follows: "If the Elephant faces a region that is already dominated by the acting region (with the Elephant’s tail), use the first clockwise region from that border where this is not true."
37: 
38: [b]Blackmail Cards:[/b]
39: + Mercantile and Diplomatic Connection Cards. If you reduce a roll to 0 dice, treat the roll as a failure. 
40: 
41: [b]Law Cards:[/b]
42: + Military Oversight. The old commander is a candidate to be the new commander as they are now an officer. 
43: 
44: [b]Rules Clarifications[/b]
45: + Out of Family Pieces. Players are now forced to cannibalize their position. The rule now reads: If you need to place a family piece but have none, you must choose to take one from any prize. If taken from a prize, lower your victory point marker by the printed value of that prize. (Note: this rule also applies to creating Firm shares in Deregulation.) 
46: + No [Family] Action. A new rule has been added to the family action page. It reads: Rarely, players may be unable to take a family action. In these cases, no action is taken and their opportunity token should be placed in their supply of pieces. In practice this only happens if a player has no family pieces, prizes, or money. 
47: [size=9][i][size=9][i]There are some truly strange situations that can emerge where players run out of pieces. This would mostly happen in the full campaign game with early deregulation and a unprofitable but still strong-ish Company. To this end I had to adjust the Family Action rules as follows:[/i][/size] Connected to that, I revised the Empty Court rule to cover situations where the game runs out of folks to be Chairman and explicitly state that it is possible for there to be no Chairman. Again, this is a crazy situation that I've never seen in well over 100 tests. But it can happen and so the rule has been added.[/i][/size]
48: 
49: + Deploy Action. You can only deploy to adjacent regions if they are not already Company-controlled. The new wording now reads: "You may select your President’s home region, a region associated with your Presidency, or a region that shares a border with a region associated with your Presidency. You cannot target another President’s home region or a Company-controlled region associated with another Presidency."
50: 
51: +Region Loss and Closing Orders. This rule now only applies to the Invasion Crisis. This narrowing is because the closing of orders already happens in both the default behavior of the Foreign Invasion and Rebellion events. 
52: 
53: In sum, these are pretty small things. I'll be sure to keep this post up to date with any interesting inquiries I happen to see either on BGG or on the discord. And, if you don't see your favorite typo or minor errata called out above, don't worry! I'll have the full list--I just want to use this thread to call any of the larger game-impacting errors that snuck in. 
54: 
55: [size=18]Revised Letter to Players[/size]
56: You can find the revised letter to players which now includes, on the reverse, some graphical examples to help new players with general board anatomy here:
57: https://www.dropbox.com/s/7o2ki5hue2ka42g/Letter%20to%20Players%202nd%20printing%20%28bgg%29.pdf?dl=0
58: 
59: [size=18]Full Errata Document[/size]
60: For the vast majority of players, the points above should address all of the outstanding errata. However, in the interest of full disclosure, here's the current internal errata document. 
61: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hvtkMaKiyhENYW7SWNoBdGQkL-FCcSFkOycgTlaGris/edit?usp=sharing
62: Note that this document is fairly technical, and mostly intended for use by myself and our language partners as we maintain the game's files. It's long and scary and most of the adjustments here are pretty minor. I'll continue to update both this document as well as this thread with any changes. And, after we finish our language localizations, I will be sure to upload a fresh 2nd Printing rulebook which has these changes folded in (I suspect we'll have this  by Christmas or sooner). Again, this document isn't the kind of thing you'd want to print and stick in the box as it's not really intended for use by players, espeically during play. But, it's here all the same in case you'd like to see how the sausage gets made. 
63: 
64: [size=18]Edit History[/size]
65: October 10th. Added a couple of items regarding setup and the family actions.
66: October 29th. Added a few rulebook clarifications and one Law Clarification. Added full errata. Board Anatomy sheet to come shortly.
67: January 3rd. Added a few clarifications to the full errata and one omission/clarification which is called out in this post. High resolution board anatomy sheet now linked.
